subject: astronomy
title: Space Exploration: Living in Space
welcome_lead: No gravity, no fresh air — yet humans live there. Here's how.
meta_desc: KS3 astronomy: microgravity, spacesuits, ISS daily life.
final_note: Space tests the limits of what humans can endure.

concepts.def: Special suit that keeps astronauts alive in space.
Reusing water and air on the ISS.
A section of a space station.

walkthroughs.body_html: In orbit, astronauts are in free fall around Earth and feel weightless. Their feet don't stay on the floor — sleeping bags strap to a wall.
A spacesuit is a personal spacecraft: air, water, temperature control and protection from tiny meteoroids. EVAs can last 6+ hours.
The ISS recycles sweat and even urine into clean drinking water. CO2 is scrubbed from the air. Resupply rockets bring food and new science.
